title: SSE reconnect hinting, semantic chunking, and deterministic reassembly
creator: Ayesha Patel
description: Implement server-side and client-facing improvements for SSE streaming to make reconnects resilient, minimize duplicated output, and preserve semantic boundaries for function/tool call frames and structured outputs. This ticket covers: 1) a reconnect hint negotiation header so clients can choose optimized backoff vs full-resume; 2) deterministic fragment ids and lightweight per-fragment checksums to allow safe reassembly and de-duplication on reconnect; 3) semantic chunking rules to avoid splitting JSON/FunctionCall blocks mid-token (tokenizer-aware boundary hints); 4) compatibility shims for existing EventStream/JSONL clients; and 5) telemetry and acceptance criteria for rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits X-Resume-Hint and X-Fragment-ID headers on streaming sessions per the new negotiation spec
Clients reconnecting with a resume token can rehydrate KV-cache and continue from last acknowledged fragment without duplicate function_call invocations in >99.9% of reconnect scenarios
No structured JSON object produced by the runtime is split across fragments unless explicitly tagged as splittable by the model harness
Backward-compatible behavior with legacy JSONL/line-delimited clients via offer of 'compat=legacy' in the handshake
Dashboard shows per-session fragment loss rate, average reconnect latency, and de-duplication rate; SLO: <0.1% customer-visible duplicated function calls after rollout
design_decisions: Use 128-bit RFC4122 v4 UUIDs for fragment IDs to avoid cross-cluster collision, but include 64-bit truncated hash as human-friendly short-id in debug logs
Resume tokens are server-signed opaque blobs containing fragment_id, session_epoch, and a short integrity MAC; we avoid exposing internal node ids
Prefer tokenizer-aware boundary hints from the model-serving side rather than client-side reconstitution to minimize client complexity
Provide two reconnect modes: 'resume' (preferred) and 'replay-safeguard' (full re-send with idempotency checks), negotiated via header
Keep the default fragment size at 4KB for hosted traffic but allow dynamic fragmentation hints based on latency SLOs and downstream throughput
tradeoffs_and_risks: Choosing tokenizer-aware chunking reduces duplicate partial JSONs but requires additional CPU during generation to compute boundaries
Signed resume tokens add complexity to key rotation; will need a small key-management story for runtime nodes
Introducing new headers may confuse some third-party proxies; compatibility shim will map X-Resume-Hint to existing EventStream semantics for known carriers
Edge-case risk: extremely long function_call arguments that legitimately exceed fragment size will be specially tagged and require client-side assembly
implementation_notes: Proposed API headers: X-Resume-Hint: resume|replay-safeguard, X-Fragment-ID: <uuid>, X-Fragment-Checksum: <hex64>, X-Compat: legacy|eventstream
Server will attach inline JSON metadata events (type:fragment-meta) as part of SSE to convey semantic boundary markers; clients that use legacy compat should ignore these events
Add server-side generation hook to the runtime to emit boundary_hint tokens aligned with our tokenizer (BPE) index; store last stable boundary in session state
On reconnect: client supplies last-seen fragment_id and preferred mode; server validates token MAC, checks session_epoch, and either streams missing fragments or resumes generation state
Where model runtime cannot produce tokenizer hints (some S2S models), fallback to newline-safe chunking and bump monitoring alert to research
test_plan: Unit tests for fragment ID generation, checksum verification, tokenized-boundary detection
Integration tests: simulated flaky network that drops connections at boundaries (0B..100KB) asserting no duplicated function_call side-effects
Compatibility tests: legacy JSONL client should successfully reconstruct full output when X-Compat=legacy is offered
Chaos tests in staging: pod kill during burst and verify resume tokens allow continuation within latency SLO
Load test: 10k concurrent SSE sessions with varied reconnect patterns to ensure fragment metadata doesn't increase CPU by >8%
rollout_plan: Canary rollout: 1% hosted traffic for 48h -> 10% for 72h -> 50% for 24h -> 100% if no regressions
During canary, instrument a synthetic canary client that intentionally reconnects at known offsets to validate end-to-end correctness
Provide 'compat=legacy' server-side mapping for customers who cannot upgrade clients; log use for deprecation planning
Customer communications: changelog, migration guide, and example client snippets in SDKs showing how to pass last-seen fragment id and preferred mode
telemetry_and_observability: New metrics: fragment_emitted_total, fragment_lost_estimate, resume_success_total, duplicate_function_call_count
Span annotations: attach fragment_id and resume_hint to request traces for quick triage
New dashboard: Streaming Resume Overview (per-model, per-region), alert on duplicate_function_call_count > 1 per 10k sessions
Log examples and runbook added at https://confluence.company/streaming/resume-v2 (placeholder for final doc)
comments: 2026-02-18 Ayesha Patel: Created ticket with initial scope after architecture sync. Asked runtime team to evaluate CPU impact of tokenizer-aware boundaries.
2026-02-22 Marco Rossi: PoC of fragment ID and checksum in runtime. Observed ~3% CPU increase for boundary hinting on small models; large models negligible. PoC PR in progress.
2026-03-01 Jun Park (review): Suggested switching to HMAC-SHA256 for resume token MAC and adding short rotation window. Also requested privacy review for token contents.

2026-03-05 Taylor Nguyen (QA): Submitted initial integration tests for flaky reconnects. Found duplicate function call in extreme case where client replays without last-seen fragment; added hardening to server validation.
2026-03-10 Marco Rossi: Implemented 'compat=legacy' mapping and added feature flag. Canary scheduled to start 2026-03-14 with synthetic clients.

2026-03-12 Ayesha Patel: Updated acceptance criteria to include SLO for duplicated function calls and added dashboard links. Removed hard dependency on KMS rotation for first canary (will schedule in follow-on ticket).
